texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 07.12.2016. The Road Traffic Accident in question took place on 17.05.2016, at about 12:10 AM near the house of the petitioner when she was sitting on the footpath near her house. She suffered grievous injuries in the said accident. The said accident was allegedly caused by the vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration No.DL-1YD-7981 which was driven by respondent No.1, Puneet, owned by respondent no. 2, Chanson Motors Pvt. Ltd. and insured with respondent no. 3, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. 2. During the course of proceedings, the petitioner/injured expired and her legal heirs i.e. Sh. Inder Pal (son); Sh. Arvind (son) and Sh. Bhudev (son) were brought on record. Brief facts of the case: 3. Based on the facts outlined in the DAR, it emerges that on 17.05.2016 at about 12:10 AM, the petitioner was sitting on the footpath near her house and suffered grievous injuries in the said accident. The said accident was allegedly caused by the vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration No.DL-1YD-7981 which was driven by respondent No.1, Puneet in a zig zag manner and hit the injured, Munni Devi due to which she fell unconscious and sustained grievous injuries. 4. Thereafter, the injured person was taken to Sushruta Trauma Centre, Civil Lines, Delhi and MLC bearing no. 225986 of the petitioner was prepared by the doctors. It is further averred that respondent nos.1, 2 and 3 being the driver, owner and insurer/insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly, severally and vicariously liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. 5. It is further averred that the accident had occurred absolutely due to rash, reckless and negligent driving of the offending vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration No. DL-1YD-7981. The IO investigated in the matter. On the basis of MLC and on completion of investigation, the chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC was filed with respect to respondent no.1 before the Ld. MM and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 07.12.2016. Written statements: 6. Respondent nos.1 and 2 did not file their respective written statements and their right to file the same was closed vide order dated 06.04.2017, however, the respondent no. 3 filed its reply. ISSUES FRAMED 7. OPP iii. Relief. EVIDENCE 8. The petitioner examined herself Munni Devi as PW-1. However, the respondents did not lead any evidence. 9. The petitioner had filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded and final arguments were heard on behalf of the petitioner and respondent no. 3. Suddenly one Car bearing no. DL-1YD-7981 was came in a very rash, negligent and high speed manner and without taking any precautions and blowing any horn and hit the petitioner, due to which the petitioner got grievous injuries in her left side body. The petitioner/injured sustained multiple grievous injuries, which is also mentioned in the MLC bearing no. 225986. Thereafter, the petitioner was taken to the Lok Nayak Hospital and petitioner/injured was medically examined and the doctors of the said hospital prepared the MLC no. 225986 and the petitioner/injured was remained admitted and operated there on 30.09.2017 but she could not get reliefs from his intolerable pain and wounds. 4. I say that the driver/respondent no. 1 was driving his offending vehicle in a very rash, negligent and careless manner, without blowing any horn, violating the rules and regulations of the traffic and brutally hit against the petitioner/injured. 6. Earlier award amount (which has already been received by the petitioner in terms of previous award passed by Ld. - Predecessor) to be deducted from present award amount . 7. Total amount including Interest Rs. 1,54,197.02/- (rounded off to Rs. 1,54,197/-) 9. The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Puneet, owned by respondent no. 2, Chanson Motor Pvt. Ltd. and insured with respondent no. 3, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Therefore, respondent nos. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent no. 3 is liable to indemnify respondent nos. 1 and 2. The said respondent is further directed to give intimation of deposit of the compensation amount to the claimant and shall file a compliance report with the Claims Tribunal with respect to the deposit of the compensation amount within 15 days of the deposit with a copy to the Claimant and his counsel. Ahlmad shall also e-mail an authenticated copy of the award to Branch Manager, SBI, Tis Hazari Courts for information.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. The treatment of the petitioner/injured has to continue further for some long time which will involve heavy future medical expenses. The petitioner/injured is not having any other source of income. The losses suffered by the injured cannot be measured in monetary terms. It is submitted that till this date, the petitioner/injured is taking continuous treatment of her grievous injuries but it may be possible that she may suffered with permanent disability in future. 10. I say that the petitioner/injured was earning her livelihood for her family members and at the time of her accident she sustained grievous and blunt injuries in roadside vehicular accident and during the treatment in the aforesaid hospital her family members have to face tremendous harassment and mental pain and the petitioner/injured and her family are very poor and had small amounts of saving which they spent on the treatment but the respondents have not given even a single penny for the treatment of the petitioner/injured. 11. It is submitted that due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1 all this happened only due to rash, negligent, car and dangerous driving of the respondent no. 1 and if, the petitioner/injured suffers with permanent disability at this stage, then the petitioner/injured and his entire family shall suffer irreparable loss and injury which cannot be compensated in terms of money. It is further submitted that the petitioner/injured is only the supporter of her entire family members and from the date of fateful incident, the petitioner/injured is lying on bed and taking treatment for her better health. The petitioner/injured and her family are very poor and hail from very poor strata of society and if this Hon'ble Court will not grant compensation for the injuries and disability which sustained by the petitioner/injured in the roadside vehicular accident, then the petitioner/injured and her entire family would come on road and shall be hand to mouth. In this regard, reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. 15. It is also settled law that the petitioner cannot be expected to prove the accident to the hilt and the principle of res ipse loquitor should apply which means that the "accident speaks for itself". 16. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC and other relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Puneet (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Munni Devi (Sr. Citizen) ... vs Puneet (Uiic) on 3 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111951897/ 9 Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and under item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. This is a case where permanent disability is claimed and compensation is also demanded qua future loss of earnings on account of permanent disability, hence, this Tribunal now proceeds further step Munni Devi (Sr. Citizen) ... vs Puneet (Uiic) on 3 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111951897/ 13 by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition. Determination of Injuries and Duration of the Treatment: 22. Further, the petitioner has claimed that she could not go to work for 6 months but there is no proof of the same. Further, the injured has now expired and as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Company Limited v Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon 2021 (4) TAC 1 (SC) , pain and suffering being a personal loss is not sustainable if the injured expires. The LRs of the petitioner have claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. Accordingly, the Multiplier of five (5) is taken for purposes of calculating the loss of income of the petitioner (Reliance is placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors., Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, date of decision - 31.10.2017). Further, by adopting the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC), the future prospects of Munni Devi shall be nil. 33. In the case of Benson George V. Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum.
